$comment: Both Illinois local rates adjust on July 1, not January 1. Chicago's tipped wage is on its own separate escalator toward abolishing the tip credit in 2028.

jurisdictions.name: Chicago

tipped.note: Chicago's tip-credit phase-out under the 2023 One Fair Wage ordinance was PAUSED at 76% by a May 2026 City Council vote -- the originally-legislated jump to 84% did not happen on 2026-07-01 as planned. $12.96 is 76% of $17.05, unchanged in percentage terms from the prior year's $12.62 (also 76%, of $16.60). The next step is now 2028-07-01 (to 84%), with full parity delayed to 2030-07-01 for most employers -- and to 2033-07-01 for small businesses (21 or fewer employees), a slower carve-out that did not exist in the ordinance's original 2023 version. CORRECTED: an earlier version of this file's note described a straight '8 points a year to 100% by 2028' schedule that stopped being true the moment the pause passed.

scheduledChanges.note: First step of the delayed schedule after the May 2026 pause. Full parity (100%) follows on 2030-07-01 for most employers; small businesses (21 or fewer employees) follow their own slower schedule, reaching parity only on 2033-07-01.

jurisdictions.name: Cook County (excluding Chicago)
jurisdictions.coverage: Suburban Cook County. The county ordinance does NOT apply inside the City of Chicago, which has its own. Individual municipalities within Cook County may opt out of the county ordinance by local ordinance -- a real coverage hole this database records but does not enumerate. Employers need at least four employees (one if the employee is a domestic worker) and a Cook County business facility or license; employees under a collective bargaining agreement, in subsidized youth or transitional programs, in their first 90 days or under 18 at the Illinois sub-minimum, camp counselors, impaired-capacity workers and licensed learners are excluded under the County's 2018 rules (Rule 3.05). The engine cannot see these facts, so the headline rate binds.

sources.title: Cook County Minimum Wage Interpretative and Procedural Rules, approved July 1, 2018 (Rules 2.01, 3.01-3.05)
sources.verifiedBy: Rule text supplied by the user on 2026-11-07 (the rules PDF is linked from the County's minimum-wage page). Rule 3.01: a Covered Employer employs at least one Covered Employee as a Domestic Worker, or at least four employees one of whom is a Covered Employee, and maintains a Business Facility in Cook County or is subject to Chapter 54 licensing; not covered: Government Employers other than Cook County, regulated motor carriers under 3(d)(7) of the Illinois Minimum Wage Law, and employers preempted by federal or state law. Rule 3.03: a Covered Employee has worked at least two hours in a two-week period in Cook County. Rule 2.01: the wage does not apply to work inside a municipality that has lawfully preempted the Ordinance. Rule 3.05, employees who are NOT Covered Employees: (1) under a bona fide collective bargaining agreement, (2) subsidized temporary youth employment programs, (3) subsidized transitional employment programs, (4) employees within Illinois Minimum Wage Law 4(a)(2) (the first 90 consecutive calendar days, up to 50 cents under the Illinois wage), (5) employees within 4(a)(3) (under 18, up to 50 cents under the Illinois wage), (6) camp counselors under 4(d) and 4(e), (7) persons with earning capacity impaired by age, disability or injury under Section 5, (8) employees licensed as learners by the Illinois Commission of Labor under Section 6 (text supplied ended after item 8; any further items were not seen). These are the 2018 rules: the 50-cent figures are as that text then described Illinois law, not re-verified against current Illinois law, and a newer County FAQ is said to describe a reduction from the County wage rather than an exclusion; that discrepancy is unresolved, so the headline County rate binds.
